subject: Evacuation schedule & pin lifecycle checklist for AcmeHealth private deployment
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Greg Walsh <greg@acmehealth.com>, soojin.lee@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 13 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Evacuation schedule & pin lifecycle checklist for AcmeHealth private deployment

Greg / team —

Following our runbook review, I want to lock in the maintenance window and the evacuation (unpin) criteria for the private deployment in your VPC. The goal is to have a short, scripted maintenance window that allows us to:

- Apply security micropatches and model runtime fixes (no model version bump unless explicitly approved)
- Validate KV cache warmup and zero-trust egress rules post-change
- Provide a tested, rehearsed rollback path (both staged unpin and full rollback)

Proposed schedule:
- Dry-run (no traffic): Thu 2028-11-23 02:00–03:00 UTC
- Live window: Fri 2028-11-24 02:00–05:00 UTC (3 hours)

Key asks for Acme ops:
1) Agree on the live window above, or propose alternate 2-hour block.
2) Confirm ability to provide BGP/peering telemetry for the 30 minutes before the window.
3) Confirm KMS key rotation policy acceptance for any agent-side certs touched.

Attached is a compact preflight checklist we will run 24h and 1h before the window. Please review and flag any gaps.

[Attachment: preflight-checklist.xlsx (xlsx) — compact checks: VIP health, peering health, DNS TTL, KMS access test, KV cache snapshot] 

If we lock this, ops and infra will run the following pin lifecycle:
- Stage pin: pin current runtime version to canary nodes only (30m)
- Evacuate: remove canary nodes from LB, validate latency and error rates (15m)
- Promote or rollback based on metrics and logs (30m)

Thanks — want to be explicit on 'evacuation' (our term for staged unpin + KV seed) to avoid surprise full-rollbacks.

—Evelyn Hart
Senior TPM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, soojin.lee@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, Greg Walsh <greg@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Nov 2028 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Evacuation schedule & pin lifecycle checklist for AcmeHealth private deployment

Thanks Evelyn — some technical notes and tweaks from runtime/ network side:

1) Window sizing: 3 hours is safe but for low-impact patches we can compress to 90–120 minutes if Acme can accept shorter verification (we still need at least 30m for KV warmup).

2) Network preflight (required):
   - Confirm private DNS responses across all AZs 10m before; TTLs must be <= 60s for quick failover.
   - Confirm firewall (NSG) config snapshot available for replay in rollback.
   - BGP flaps: if peers show >3 route withdrawals in 5m before window, abort.

3) Pin lifecycle detail:
   - Pin to canary: pin config applied to 2-3 canary nodes in each region, not across the whole fleet.
   - KV snapshot: take consistent snapshot and store encrypted to customer S3 (or their internal blob store).
   - Evac criteria: 2000 tokens/s per node degradation threshold OR 1.5x tail latency increase OR any 5xx spikes >0.5% over baseline.

4) Rollback variants:
   - Fast-rollback (preferred): revert pin on canary, reattach canaries; verified in 10–15m.
   - Emergency full rollback: if canary rollback fails, trigger full fleet pin reversion (requires coordination with Acme netops for LB drain, estimated 45–60m).

I added a small change to the preflight sheet: explicit 'KMS test with rotated key id' and 'agent cert verify via new key' rows.

On the timeline: I can be on call for the dry-run and live window; Soojin, Monica — please confirm ops coverage.

—Karthik
Principal Architect, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Evelyn / Karthik —

Thanks — the Friday window (2028-11-24 02:00–05:00 UTC) works for us if we keep the live changes limited to the runtime micropatch and not move model pins. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- We can provide BGP/peering telemetry but need a 2-hour notice to open the drain window on our side.
- We cannot accept a full-fleet rollback without a written postmortem commitment; for emergency full rollback we will require a 1-hour coordination call before execution (we understand this adds time).
- Our KMS policy: we won't rotate keys during the maintenance; we can allow a key test against the existing key id.

If we accept the compressed 120 minute live window, we want the first 30m for pre-change verification (DNS, certs, telemetry), 60m for change + canary validation, 30m for extend/fallback. That maps cleanly to your canary/pin plan.

We are OK with the proposed evacuation thresholds. Please note we will require the KV snapshot be encrypted with our customer-managed CMK and the snapshot integrity hash shared post-run.

—Greg
VP Platform, AcmeHealth

All —

Per Karthik and Greg we will compress to the 120m live window and add the extra coordination call for any full-fleet rollback. Finalized ops plan below (short checklist + ownership):

Preflight (24h):
- Acme to confirm RBAC and KMS access (Greg) — done
- Redwood: run DNS and peering smoke tests in staging (Monica) — in progress

T-minus 1h checklist (Ops run in order):
1) Snapshot KV and push encrypted object to s3://acme-redwood-snapshots (Monica)
2) Verify private DNS TTLs across AZs (Sooj)
3) Export firewall snapshot and stage rollback command set (Sooj)
4) Start 30m BGP telemetry capture (Acme)

During window (minute markers):
- 00:00–00:30: pre-change verification (DNS, certs, BGP stability) — SRE/Acme on call
- 00:30–01:30: apply pinned micropatch to canaries + KV warmup validation
- 01:30–02:00: monitor metrics for target thresholds; either promote or trigger rollback

Rollback matrix:
- Canary rollback: automated pin revert script (k8s-job) — target revert 10–15m (Sooj owns)
- Full rollback: require lead-to-lead conference call (Evelyn + Greg + Karthik) — estimated 45–60m

Attachments: finalized runbook excerpt and the rollback markdown that contains exact revert commands and the firewall replay snippets.

[Attachment: rollback-runbook.md (markdown) — contains revert scripts, iptables/NSG replay, and k8s pin revert job] 

I'll upload the final runbook + the annotated checklist to the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcX_preflight_docs

If no objections by EOD, Monica and I will schedule the dry-run on Nov 23 and the live window Nov 24.

—Soojin Lee
Ops Lead, Customer Deployments
Redwood Inference
